messages.subject: sigma and phi symbol in statistics
parts:
Hi all

I need to learn the rules that govern on sigma (Σ) and pi (Π) symbols in statistics. can any one introduce to me some books or references (intermediate and advance level) that teach rules for sigma and pi symbol? any help?

Best

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: sigma and phi symbol in statistics

Speaking only for myself, I don't understand the question. Assuming
this is a serious question and not a troll, you may want to give some
more background as to what you're trying to accomplish.

And for the record, Wikipedia has a wealth of information, including
references, about various topics in statistics, including, in
particular, the two items you mention.

Also for the record, I used an early edition of DeGroot and Schervish:

https://www.amazon.com/Probability-Statistics-5th-Morris-DeGroot/dp/0134687000/ref=dp_ob_title_bk

and found it to be useful.

messages.author: 1ec981f6ad974842
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: sigma and phi symbol in statistics
parts:
I actually sympathize with this question, and I doubt it's a troll - if you've never had training in mathematics and then take some advanced statistics classes, the use of these symbols is often taken for granted.  If your'e lost, the answer of course is to go back to fundamentals, the best explanations of which you're more likely to find in basic and advanced mathematics references, not statistics ones.

As I understand them, the symbol for sigma (Σ) refers to summation, while pi (Π) refers to a product.  Hope that gets you started.

messages.author: d567d0ef3c054a35
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: sigma and phi symbol in statistics
parts:
Ah, I see I was overthinking this. I really don't know where you
would find more than a very-brief description of those topics,
although I suppose there must be books that talk about them in some
detail. (When I studied this stuff the Greeks didn't yet have an
alphabet.)

But let me add:

(1) I still think the web is a good place to look for discussions of
summations and products.

(2) This is indeed not really a topic for this mailing list (but a
friend in need is a friend indeed).

(3) If you don't already know a programming language, you should
probably learn one, if for no other reason than that you could then
get authoritative answers to questions you might have. As a trivial
example, in R (the subject of this list) you can compute sums and
products:

> sum(1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8)
[1] 20
> prod(1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8)
[1] 240
>

So, come up with a paper-and-pencil solution, then check it with R (or
Python or ...).

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: sigma and phi symbol in statistics
parts:
The Khan academy intro on the subject might help you out. Π notation is identical to sigma notation, except instead of adding the numbers in the sequence, you multiply them.

https://www.khanacademy.org/math/algebra2/sequences-and-series/alg2-sigma-notation/v/sigma-notation-sum

Thanks,
Erica

Ph.D. Candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis
